widgets.title: Database Availability Uptime %
widgets.description: Availability (available) is a point-in-time signal: "can I reach this database right now?" It's a binary 0 or 1 captured each collection cycle.

nrqlQueries.query: SELECT percentage(count(*), WHERE available = 1) AS 'Uptime %' FROM PostgresqlHealthSample WHERE checkType IN ({{checkType}}) AND checkType != 'query' AND displayName IN ({{instance}}) AND label.service_name IN ({{service_name}}) AND label.role IN ({{role}}) AND label.environment IN ({{environment}}) TIMESERIES FACET displayName

widgets.title: Health Check Error Rate
widgets.description: Error rate across all check types (implicit, explicit, query). A non-zero rate indicates connectivity, auth, or query issues.

nrqlQueries.query: SELECT percentage(count(*), WHERE hasError = 1) AS 'Error Rate %' FROM PostgresqlHealthSample WHERE displayName IN ({{instance}}) AND checkType IN ({{checkType}}) AND label.service_name IN ({{service_name}}) AND label.role IN ({{role}}) AND label.environment IN ({{environment}})

widgets.title: DB Fleet Status
widgets.description: How many instances are reporting and their current availability state.

nrqlQueries.query: SELECT uniqueCount(displayName) as 'total instances', filter(uniqueCount(displayName), WHERE available = 1) AS 'up', filter(uniqueCount(displayName), WHERE available = 0) AS 'down' FROM PostgresqlHealthSample WHERE checkType IN ({{checkType}}) AND checkType != 'query' AND displayName IN ({{instance}}) AND label.service_name IN ({{service_name}}) AND label.role IN ({{role}}) AND label.environment IN ({{environment}}) SINCE 10 minutes ago

rawConfiguration.text:
## Database Availability & Uptime
---

#### Availability
A **point-in-time** signal captured each collection cycle: *can I reach this database right now?*

All checks emit `PostgresqlHealthSample` with a `checkType` attribute:

| checkType | Method | What it proves |
|---|---|---|
| **implicit** | PostgreSQL protocol ping | Server is listening and responds at the wire level |
| **explicit** | Canary SQL query (e.g. `SELECT 1`) | Query parser, execution engine, and auth layer are functional |
| **query** | Internal monitoring queries | Individual query health and duration |

> Implicit is lightweight but won't catch connection exhaustion or permission issues. Explicit exercises the full query path.

---

#### Uptime %
Availability **aggregated over a time window** — what fraction of checks succeeded?

Uptime % = (successful checks / total checks) × 100

At a **10s interval** over 5 minutes ≈ 30 checks. If 1 fails → **96.7% uptime**.

> **Important:** These checks measure availability from the integration’s perspective using a single monitoring user. Not every error means the database is down for all consumers. For example, a `pg_error_28` (authentication failure) may indicate a credential issue specific to the monitoring user while the database remains fully available to application traffic. This makes availability monitoring a strong proxy for uptime, but not a guarantee — treat it as one signal alongside application-level health checks.

---

#### Connection Timing (implicit only)

| Metric | Definition |
|---|---|
| **`dnsLookupMs`** | Time to resolve the hostname to an IP via DNS |
| **`tcpConnectMs`** | Time for the TCP three-way handshake to the resolved IP |
| **`tlsHandshakeMs`** | Time for the TLS/SSL negotiation (only when SSL is enabled) |

> A spike in DNS or TCP time indicates infrastructure issues, not PostgreSQL. A spike in `tlsHandshakeMs` suggests certificate chain or negotiation issues. A spike in `durationMs` with normal connection timing suggests PostgreSQL-level contention.

---

#### Error Codes

See [PostgreSQL Error Codes](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/errcodes-appendix.html) for full SQLSTATE reference.

| Code | Cause |
|---|---|
| `timeout` | Query or connection exceeded deadline |
| `pg_error_28` | Authentication failure ([SQLSTATE class 28](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/errcodes-appendix.html#ERRCODES-TABLE)) |
| `pg_error_42` | Syntax / permission error ([SQLSTATE class 42](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/errcodes-appendix.html#ERRCODES-TABLE)) |
| `pg_error_57` | Query canceled / admin shutdown ([SQLSTATE class 57](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/errcodes-appendix.html#ERRCODES-TABLE)) |
| `connection_refused` | Server not listening |
| `dns_resolution_failed` | Hostname cannot be resolved |
| `tls_error` | Certificate or TLS handshake failure |

---

#### Resources
- [PostgreSQL SSL/TLS Support](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/ssl-tcp.html)
- [PostgreSQL Error Codes](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/errcodes-appendix.html)
- [pg_stat_activity](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/monitoring-stats.html#MONITORING-PG-STAT-ACTIVITY-VIEW)
- [nri-postgresql Integration](https://docs.newrelic.com/docs/infrastructure/host-integrations/host-integrations-list/postgresql-monitoring-integration/)
- [NRQL Reference](https://docs.newrelic.com/docs/nrql/get-started/introduction-nrql-new-relics-query-language/)

widgets.title: Uptime % Over Time
widgets.description: Database Availability by Instance over time

nrqlQueries.query: SELECT percentage(count(*), WHERE available = 1) AS 'Uptime %' FROM PostgresqlHealthSample WHERE checkType IN ({{checkType}}) AND checkType != 'query' AND displayName IN ({{instance}}) AND label.service_name IN ({{service_name}}) AND label.role IN ({{role}}) AND label.environment IN ({{environment}}) TIMESERIES FACET displayName

widgets.title: Response Time Max ms (DNS + TCP + TLS + Total)
widgets.description: Connection phase breakdown: DNS resolution, TCP handshake, TLS negotiation, and total query duration across implicit and explicit checks.

nrqlQueries.query: SELECT max(dnsLookupMs) AS 'dnsLookup', max(tcpConnectMs) AS 'tcpConnect', max(tlsHandshakeMs) AS 'tlsHandshake', max(durationMs) AS 'total' FROM PostgresqlHealthSample WHERE checkType IN ({{checkType}}) AND checkType != 'query' AND displayName IN ({{instance}}) AND label.service_name IN ({{service_name}}) AND label.role IN ({{role}}) AND label.environment IN ({{environment}}) TIMESERIES FACET displayName

widgets.title: Slowest Internal Queries — avg (ms)
widgets.description: Top internal monitoring queries by average duration. High values may indicate PostgreSQL server pressure.

nrqlQueries.query: SELECT average(durationMs) AS 'avg' FROM PostgresqlHealthSample WHERE checkType = 'query' AND displayName IN ({{instance}}) AND label.service_name IN ({{service_name}}) AND label.role IN ({{role}}) AND label.environment IN ({{environment}}) FACET queryName LIMIT 15

widgets.title: Query Duration Over Time — avg (ms)
widgets.description: Internal monitoring query performance trends. Spikes correlate with PostgreSQL load.

nrqlQueries.query: SELECT average(durationMs) AS 'avg', percentile(durationMs, 95) AS 'p95' FROM PostgresqlHealthSample WHERE checkType = 'query' AND displayName IN ({{instance}}) AND label.service_name IN ({{service_name}}) AND label.role IN ({{role}}) AND label.environment IN ({{environment}}) FACET displayName TIMESERIES AUTO

widgets.title: Availability by Service
widgets.description: Uptime grouped by service_name — useful for comparing health across deploys.

nrqlQueries.query: SELECT percentage(count(*), WHERE available = 1) AS 'Uptime %' FROM PostgresqlHealthSample WHERE checkType IN ({{checkType}}) AND checkType != 'query' AND displayName IN ({{instance}}) AND label.service_name IN ({{service_name}}) AND label.role IN ({{role}}) AND label.environment IN ({{environment}}) FACET label.service_name

widgets.title: Availability by AZ
widgets.description: Uptime grouped by availability zone — surfaces zone-specific outages.

nrqlQueries.query: SELECT percentage(count(*), WHERE available = 1) AS 'Uptime %' FROM PostgresqlHealthSample WHERE checkType IN ({{checkType}}) AND checkType != 'query' AND displayName IN ({{instance}}) AND label.service_name IN ({{service_name}}) AND label.role IN ({{role}}) AND label.environment IN ({{environment}}) FACET label.availability_zone

widgets.title: Errors Over Time
widgets.description: Error count by classified error code across all check types.

nrqlQueries.query: SELECT count(*) FROM PostgresqlHealthSample WHERE hasError = 1 AND displayName IN ({{instance}}) AND checkType IN ({{checkType}}) AND label.service_name IN ({{service_name}}) AND label.role IN ({{role}}) AND label.environment IN ({{environment}}) FACET errorCode, displayName TIMESERIES AUTO

widgets.title: Error Breakdown
widgets.description: Distribution of errors by type.

nrqlQueries.query: SELECT count(*) FROM PostgresqlHealthSample WHERE hasError = 1 AND displayName IN ({{instance}}) AND checkType IN ({{checkType}}) AND label.service_name IN ({{service_name}}) AND label.role IN ({{role}}) AND label.environment IN ({{environment}}) FACET errorCode

widgets.title: Recent Errors
widgets.description: Most recent error per unique error code combination.

nrqlQueries.query: SELECT latest(errorMessage), latest(durationMs), latest(checkType) FROM PostgresqlHealthSample WHERE hasError = 1 AND displayName IN ({{instance}}) AND checkType IN ({{checkType}}) AND label.service_name IN ({{service_name}}) AND label.role IN ({{role}}) AND label.environment IN ({{environment}}) FACET errorCode, displayName

widgets.title: Health Check Configuration
widgets.description: Active check types and canary queries per monitored instance.

nrqlQueries.query: SELECT latest(query), latest(label.role), latest(label.service_name), latest(label.availability_zone), latest(label.environment), latest(database) FROM PostgresqlHealthSample WHERE displayName IN ({{instance}}) AND label.service_name IN ({{service_name}}) AND label.role IN ({{role}}) AND label.environment IN ({{environment}}) FACET displayName SINCE 30 minutes ago

widgets.title: Fleet Uptime %
widgets.description: Aggregate uptime across all instances — not faceted.

nrqlQueries.query: SELECT percentage(count(*), WHERE available = 1) AS 'Uptime %' FROM PostgresqlHealthSample WHERE checkType IN ({{checkType}}) AND checkType != 'query' AND displayName IN ({{instance}}) AND label.service_name IN ({{service_name}}) AND label.role IN ({{role}}) AND label.environment IN ({{environment}})

## Server Internals
---

Metrics from PostgreSQL's background writer and I/O subsystem.

#### Key Indicators

| Metric | What to watch |
|---|---|
| **Checkpoints** | Frequent *requested* checkpoints indicate WAL pressure — consider increasing `checkpoint_completion_target` or `max_wal_size` |
| **Backend writes** | High backend buffer writes mean the bgwriter isn't keeping up — tune `bgwriter_lru_maxpages` |
| **Buffer allocation** | Sustained high allocation rates may indicate insufficient `shared_buffers` |
| **Checkpoint timing** | Long sync times suggest I/O bottleneck on the storage layer |

---

#### Resources
- [pg_stat_bgwriter](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/monitoring-stats.html#MONITORING-PG-STAT-BGWRITER-VIEW)
- [WAL Configuration](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/wal-configuration.html)
- [Background Writer](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/runtime-config-resource.html#RUNTIME-CONFIG-RESOURCE-BACKGROUND-WRITER)

widgets.title: Checkpoints — scheduled vs requested
widgets.description: Scheduled checkpoints are normal. Requested checkpoints indicate WAL pressure.

nrqlQueries.query: SELECT rate(sum(bgwriter.checkpointsScheduledPerSecond), 1 minute) AS 'scheduled', rate(sum(bgwriter.checkpointsRequestedPerSecond), 1 minute) AS 'requested' FROM PostgresqlInstanceSample WHERE displayName IN ({{instance}}) TIMESERIES AUTO

widgets.title: Checkpoint Write + Sync Time (ms)
widgets.description: High sync times indicate storage I/O bottleneck.

nrqlQueries.query: SELECT average(bgwriter.checkpointWriteTimeInMillisecondsPerSecond) AS 'write', average(bgwriter.checkpointSyncTimeInMillisecondsPerSecond) AS 'sync' FROM PostgresqlInstanceSample WHERE displayName IN ({{instance}}) TIMESERIES AUTO

widgets.title: Buffer Writes — bgwriter vs backend
widgets.description: Backend writes should be low. If backend > bgwriter, tune bgwriter_lru_maxpages.

nrqlQueries.query: SELECT average(bgwriter.buffersWrittenByBackgroundWriterPerSecond) AS 'bgwriter', average(bgwriter.buffersWrittenByBackendPerSecond) AS 'backend', average(bgwriter.buffersWrittenForCheckpointsPerSecond) AS 'checkpoint' FROM PostgresqlInstanceSample WHERE displayName IN ({{instance}}) TIMESERIES AUTO

widgets.title: Buffers Allocated / sec
widgets.description: Sustained high allocation may indicate insufficient shared_buffers.

nrqlQueries.query: SELECT average(bgwriter.buffersAllocatedPerSecond) AS 'allocated' FROM PostgresqlInstanceSample WHERE displayName IN ({{instance}}) TIMESERIES AUTO

widgets.title: Backend Fsync Calls / sec
widgets.description: Should be near zero. Non-zero means backends are forced to fsync — bgwriter can't keep up.

nrqlQueries.query: SELECT average(bgwriter.backendFsyncCallsPerSecond) AS 'fsync' FROM PostgresqlInstanceSample WHERE displayName IN ({{instance}}) TIMESERIES AUTO

widgets.title: Background Writer Stops / sec
widgets.description: Stops indicate bgwriter hit bgwriter_lru_maxpages limit.

nrqlQueries.query: SELECT average(bgwriter.backgroundWriterStopsPerSecond) AS 'stops' FROM PostgresqlInstanceSample WHERE displayName IN ({{instance}}) TIMESERIES AUTO

rawConfiguration.text:
## Workload & Throughput
---

Per-database activity from [pg_stat_database](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/monitoring-stats.html#MONITORING-PG-STAT-DATABASE-VIEW).

#### Key Ratios

| Metric | Healthy | Investigate |
|---|---|---|
| **Cache hit ratio** | > 99% | < 95% — shared_buffers may be too small |
| **Commit ratio** | > 99% | < 95% — high rollback rate suggests app errors |
| **Rows fetched / returned** | Close to 1:1 | Large gap means many rows scanned but few used — missing indexes |

#### Deadlocks & Temp Files

- **Deadlocks** should be 0 in steady state. Persistent deadlocks indicate lock ordering issues.
- **Temp files** are created when `work_mem` is too small for sorts/joins. Frequent creation means tuning is needed.

---

#### Resources
- [pg_stat_database](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/monitoring-stats.html#MONITORING-PG-STAT-DATABASE-VIEW)
- [Tuning shared_buffers](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/runtime-config-resource.html#GUC-SHARED-BUFFERS)
- [Tuning work_mem](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/runtime-config-resource.html#GUC-WORK-MEM)

widgets.title: Connections (active / max)
widgets.description: Watch for active approaching max — connections exhaustion causes outages.

nrqlQueries.query: SELECT latest(db.connections) AS 'active', latest(db.maxconnections) AS 'max' FROM PostgresqlDatabaseSample FACET displayName TIMESERIES AUTO

widgets.title: Cache Hit Ratio %
widgets.description: Should be > 99%. Below 95% suggests shared_buffers is too small.

nrqlQueries.query: SELECT 100 * sum(db.bufferHitsPerSecond) / (sum(db.bufferHitsPerSecond) + sum(db.readsPerSecond) + 0.001) AS 'hit ratio' FROM PostgresqlDatabaseSample FACET displayName TIMESERIES AUTO

widgets.title: Transaction Rate — commits vs rollbacks
widgets.description: High rollback rate relative to commits indicates application-level errors.

nrqlQueries.query: SELECT average(db.commitsPerSecond) AS 'commits', average(db.rollbacksPerSecond) AS 'rollbacks' FROM PostgresqlDatabaseSample FACET displayName TIMESERIES AUTO

widgets.title: Row Activity — inserts / updates / deletes
widgets.description: Baseline for normal write activity. Spikes may correlate with batch jobs.

nrqlQueries.query: SELECT average(db.rowsInsertedPerSecond) AS 'inserts', average(db.rowsUpdatedPerSecond) AS 'updates', average(db.rowsDeletedPerSecond) AS 'deletes' FROM PostgresqlDatabaseSample FACET displayName TIMESERIES AUTO

widgets.title: Rows Returned vs Fetched
widgets.description: Large gap between returned and fetched suggests missing indexes — many rows scanned but few used.

nrqlQueries.query: SELECT average(db.rowsReturnedPerSecond) AS 'returned', average(db.rowsFetchedPerSecond) AS 'fetched' FROM PostgresqlDatabaseSample FACET displayName TIMESERIES AUTO

widgets.title: Deadlocks / sec
widgets.description: Should be 0. Non-zero indicates lock contention.

nrqlQueries.query: SELECT average(db.deadlocksPerSecond) AS 'deadlocks/s' FROM PostgresqlDatabaseSample FACET displayName

widgets.title: Temp Files Created / sec
widgets.description: High rate means work_mem is too small for sorts/joins.

nrqlQueries.query: SELECT average(db.tempFilesCreatedPerSecond) AS 'temp files/s' FROM PostgresqlDatabaseSample FACET displayName

widgets.title: Temp Bytes Written / sec
widgets.description: Correlates with temp file creation. Large values confirm work_mem tuning opportunity.

nrqlQueries.query: SELECT average(db.tempWrittenInBytesPerSecond) AS 'bytes/s' FROM PostgresqlDatabaseSample FACET displayName TIMESERIES AUTO

widgets.title: I/O Time — read vs write (ms/s)
widgets.description: Time spent on physical I/O. High values indicate storage saturation.

nrqlQueries.query: SELECT average(db.readTimeInMillisecondsPerSecond) AS 'read', average(db.writeTimeInMillisecondsPerSecond) AS 'write' FROM PostgresqlDatabaseSample FACET displayName TIMESERIES AUTO

widgets.title: Conflict Rate (replicas)
widgets.description: Only relevant on streaming replicas. Non-zero indicates replication conflicts.

nrqlQueries.query: SELECT average(db.conflicts.locksPerSecond) AS 'locks', average(db.conflicts.snapshotPerSecond) AS 'snapshot', average(db.conflicts.deadlockPerSecond) AS 'deadlock' FROM PostgresqlDatabaseSample FACET displayName TIMESERIES AUTO

rawConfiguration.text:
## Tables & Indexes
---

Per-table and per-index statistics from [pg_stat_user_tables](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/monitoring-stats.html#MONITORING-PG-STAT-ALL-TABLES-VIEW) and [pg_stat_user_indexes](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/monitoring-stats.html#MONITORING-PG-STAT-ALL-INDEXES-VIEW).

#### Scan Types

| Scan | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Sequential** | Full table scan — fine for small tables, costly for large ones |
| **Index** | Uses an index to find rows — efficient |

A high seq scan rate on large tables is a strong signal for a missing index.

#### Dead Rows & Vacuuming

Dead rows accumulate from UPDATE/DELETE. Autovacuum reclaims them.
- **dead rows / live rows > 10%** — autovacuum may be falling behind
- **Long time since last vacuum** — check autovacuum settings

#### Bloat

Table bloat ratio shows wasted space from dead rows not yet reclaimed. High bloat (> 50%) degrades scan performance.

---

#### Resources
- [Routine Vacuuming](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/routine-vacuuming.html)
- [Index Types](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/indexes-types.html)
- [EXPLAIN Basics](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/using-explain.html)

widgets.title: Largest Tables by Size
widgets.description: Largest tables by total size (data + indexes + TOAST).

nrqlQueries.query: SELECT latest(table.totalSizeInBytes) / 1e6 AS 'size MB' FROM PostgresqlTableSample FACET database, schema, displayName LIMIT 15

widgets.title: Sequential vs Index Scans / sec
widgets.description: Index scans should dominate. High seq scans on large tables = missing indexes.

nrqlQueries.query: SELECT sum(table.sequentialScansPerSecond) AS 'seq scans', sum(table.indexScansPerSecond) AS 'idx scans' FROM PostgresqlTableSample TIMESERIES AUTO

widgets.title: Dead Rows — top tables
widgets.description: Tables with high dead rows need vacuum attention.

nrqlQueries.query: SELECT latest(table.deadRows) AS 'dead rows' FROM PostgresqlTableSample FACET database, schema, displayName LIMIT 15

widgets.title: Table Bloat Ratio — top tables
widgets.description: Bloat > 50% degrades performance. Consider VACUUM FULL or pg_repack.

nrqlQueries.query: SELECT latest(table.bloatRatio) AS 'bloat %' FROM PostgresqlTableSample WHERE table.bloatRatio IS NOT NULL FACET database, schema, displayName LIMIT 15

widgets.title: Row Writes — inserts / updates / deletes
widgets.description: Write activity across all monitored tables.

nrqlQueries.query: SELECT sum(table.rowsInsertedPerSecond) AS 'inserts', sum(table.rowsUpdatedPerSecond) AS 'updates', sum(table.rowsDeletedPerSecond) AS 'deletes' FROM PostgresqlTableSample TIMESERIES AUTO

widgets.title: Index Size — top indexes
widgets.description: Largest indexes. Unused large indexes waste space and slow writes.

nrqlQueries.query: SELECT latest(index.sizeInBytes) / 1e6 AS 'size MB' FROM PostgresqlIndexSample FACET database, schema, displayName, index_name LIMIT 15

widgets.title: Index Reads vs Fetches / sec
widgets.description: Index read = entries scanned, fetched = rows returned. Large gap = inefficient index.

nrqlQueries.query: SELECT sum(index.rowsReadPerSecond) AS 'read', sum(index.rowsFetchedPerSecond) AS 'fetched' FROM PostgresqlIndexSample TIMESERIES AUTO

rawConfiguration.text:
## Replication
---

Metrics from custom queries against `pg_stat_replication` (primary) and `pg_stat_wal_receiver` (replica).

#### How it works

The integration runs three custom SQL queries each cycle:

1. **`pg_is_in_recovery()`** — returns `0` on primaries, `1` on replicas. Tracks server role so dashboards can detect failovers.
2. **`pg_stat_replication`** — queried on the primary. Returns one row per connected replica with replication lag in bytes.
3. **`pg_stat_wal_receiver`** — queried on the replica. Confirms streaming is active and shows pending WAL bytes.

These use the `CUSTOM_METRICS_CONFIG` flag pointing to `custom-queries.yml`. Results appear as `PgCustomQuerySample` events.

---

#### Key Indicators

| Metric | Healthy | Investigate |
|---|---|---|
| **Replication lag** | < 1 MB | > 10 MB sustained — replica can't keep up |
| **WAL receiver** | `streaming` | `catchup` or missing — check network/replica load |
| **Recovery mode** | Stable 0 or 1 | Value flips — failover occurred |

---

#### Resources
- [pg_stat_replication](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/monitoring-stats.html#MONITORING-PG-STAT-REPLICATION-VIEW)
- [pg_stat_wal_receiver](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/monitoring-stats.html#MONITORING-PG-STAT-WAL-RECEIVER-VIEW)
- [Streaming Replication](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/warm-standby.html#STREAMING-REPLICATION)
- [pg_is_in_recovery()](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/functions-info.html#FUNCTIONS-RECOVERY-INFO-TABLE)

widgets.title: Server Role
widgets.description: 0 = primary, 1 = replica. A change indicates failover.

nrqlQueries.query: SELECT latest(metric_value) AS 'in recovery' FROM PgCustomQuerySample WHERE metric_name = 'pg.isInRecovery' FACET displayName, server_role

widgets.title: WAL Receiver Status
widgets.description: 1 = streaming (healthy). 0 or missing = replication broken.

nrqlQueries.query: SELECT latest(metric_value) AS 'active' FROM PgCustomQuerySample WHERE metric_name = 'pg.walReceiver.active' FACET displayName, receiver_status

widgets.title: Replication Lag (bytes)
widgets.description: Bytes of WAL the replica is behind. Should be low and stable.

nrqlQueries.query: SELECT max(metric_value) AS 'lag bytes' FROM PgCustomQuerySample WHERE metric_name = 'pg.replication.lagBytes' FACET replica_name TIMESERIES AUTO

widgets.title: Replication Lag Over Time
widgets.description: Same as lag bytes but in MB for readability at scale.

nrqlQueries.query: SELECT max(metric_value) / 1e6 AS 'lag MB' FROM PgCustomQuerySample WHERE metric_name = 'pg.replication.lagBytes' FACET replica_name TIMESERIES AUTO

widgets.title: Server Role Over Time
widgets.description: Tracks recovery mode over time. A flip from 0→1 or 1→0 indicates a failover event.

nrqlQueries.query: SELECT latest(metric_value) AS 'in recovery' FROM PgCustomQuerySample WHERE metric_name = 'pg.isInRecovery' FACET displayName TIMESERIES AUTO

widgets.title: Replication Details
widgets.description: Per-replica replication details from the primary.

nrqlQueries.query: SELECT latest(metric_value) AS 'lag bytes', latest(replication_state), latest(sync_mode), latest(replica_addr) FROM PgCustomQuerySample WHERE metric_name = 'pg.replication.lagBytes' FACET replica_name

widgets.title: WAL Receiver Details
widgets.description: WAL receiver status from the replica's perspective.

nrqlQueries.query: SELECT latest(metric_value) AS 'active', latest(receiver_status), latest(sender_host), latest(pending_bytes) AS 'pending bytes' FROM PgCustomQuerySample WHERE metric_name = 'pg.walReceiver.active' FACET displayName
